qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI designates Astra at the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: OpenAI states Astra meets its Critical cybersecurity capability threshold because, with suitable tools and access, it can find previously unknown security flaws and develop exploits across many well-protected systems without step-by-step human guidance. OpenAI delayed parts of development and release, applied stronger cyber-abuse refusal training, cross-conversation monitoring, misalignment monitoring, and limited advanced cybersecurity access to initial testers and Daybreak Blue expansion.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: official product safety and release-gate disclosure
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Astra pre-release; advanced cybersecurity capabilities restricted at launch.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete frontier-model release gate for cyber-critical capability, with explicit containment, monitoring, and access-control controls that should inform local release-gate and cyber-evaluation pages.

qualifying_findings.title: CISA adds LiteLLM MCP authentication bypass to KEV
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: LiteLLM before 1.84.0 allowed an unauthenticated attacker to send a fabricated Authorization header to the MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint, trigger OAuth2 passthrough fallback, replace failed LiteLLM key validation with an empty UserAPIKeyAuth object, and reach MCP tooling without a valid LiteLLM key. CISA marked exploitation active and added the issue to KEV on 2026-09-02.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: government vulnerability database and exploited-vulnerability catalog with vendor advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: BerriAI LiteLLM versions before 1.84.0; MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The issue converts a model gateway's MCP endpoint into an unauthenticated tool-access path and has active-exploitation evidence, making it a priority for MCP auth and gateway pages.

upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: MCP authentication bypass, active exploitation, and mitigation to 1.84.0.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD plus CISA KEV. Original publication predates the window, but the CISA KEV addition and NVD modification are in-window concrete security changes.

qualifying_findings.title: LiteLLM proxy can leak configured provider credentials through user-controlled routing
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: LiteLLM before 1.88.6 and 1.96.2 allowed any authenticated proxy user to redirect outbound provider calls to a user-controlled destination and cause the proxy to send configured provider credentials. Incomplete validation covered request fields such as api_base, base_url, model_list, fallbacks, and litellm_credential_name across nested request fields, path values, and bracket-notation form data.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Provider keys inside model-routing proxies are high-value cross-boundary secrets; this record belongs in AI gateway credential and SSRF routing controls.

qualifying_findings.title: Windows ML CLI localhost API can enable trust-remote-code RCE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Windows ML CLI before 0.4.0 exposes CLI commands through a localhost HTTP API without authentication and configures wildcard CORS origins. A malicious website can send cross-origin requests to build or config endpoints, set trust_remote_code to true, and reach AutoConfig.from_pretrained with trust_remote_code=True, importing Python code from an attacker-controlled model repository.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Windows ML CLI before 0.4.0; localhost HTTP API.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This joins browser-origin abuse, localhost control planes, and model-repository code execution in one AI development-runtime boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent shared agent bundle overwrite leads to authenticated runner RCE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: An authenticated user with edit access to their own Omnigent session can upload a full agent bundle through PUT /sessions/{session_id}/agent and overwrite a shared/template agent even though shared agents are not intended to be MCP-editable. Adding a stdio MCP server to the shared agent can make future runner sessions start an attacker-controlled command.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: omnigent pip package before 0.3.0; shared/template agent bundle upload route.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Shared agent templates are delegated execution roots; overwriting them turns session-level edit rights into code execution for later users.

upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Agent-template ownership boundary and runner RCE.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from GitHub Advisory Database; NVD enrichment may lag.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent uploaded agent bundle allows authenticated Python callable runner RCE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: GitHub Advisory Database reports that Omnigent before 0.3.0 permits authenticated runner RCE through uploaded agent bundles and Python callable tools.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: omnigent pip package before 0.3.0; uploaded agent bundles and Python callable tools.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent bundles that define callable tools are executable supply-chain artifacts; upload paths need trust, review, and runtime isolation controls.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent shell-command parser fails open and bypasses guardrail policy
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 has a shared shell-command parser that can fail open. When a gated command is not recognized, the parser emits no operation, policy evaluation abstains, and the command is allowed, bypassing GitHub repository or branch allowlists and working-directory confinement.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Parser mismatch in agent command-approval systems can turn policy gaps into writes, pushes, workspace escapes, or exfiltration by prompt-injected agents.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent agent bundle cwd value can escape runner workspace containment
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 accepts an unvalidated os_env.cwd value in an agent bundle, yielding arbitrary host filesystem access on runners without OMNIGENT_RUNNER_WORKSPACE.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: omnigent pip package before 0.3.0; runner workspace cwd handling.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Runner workspace containment is a core boundary for delegated autonomous action; cwd authority inside imported agent bundles should not select host paths.

qualifying_findings.title: ModelScope unsafe YAML loader enables model-configuration RCE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: ModelScope uses PyYAML's unsafe yaml.Loader to parse model configuration files. Attackers can craft malicious model repositories with Python object construction tags that execute code when loaded.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ModelScope model configuration loading; affected version not fully resolved in fetched NVD summary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model repositories are executable supply-chain surfaces when runtime loaders execute configuration files; this belongs in model-artifact supply-chain controls.

qualifying_findings.title: TOON decoder prototype pollution affects LLM prompt serialization
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: TOON before 2.3.1, a compact JSON serialization for LLM prompts, wrote attacker-controlled __proto__, constructor, or prototype keys through the object prototype chain during decoding. Services decoding untrusted TOON could experience denial of service or remote code execution when a downstream gadget is present.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: TOON before 2.3.1; decoder expandPaths safe path and insertPathSafe function.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt serialization formats are part of the model-input supply chain; decoding untrusted prompt artifacts can cross from data parsing into runtime compromise.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: TOON as a prompt/data serialization entity if durable coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Prototype pollution in prompt serialization and untrusted decoder boundaries.

qualifying_findings.title: Tencent AI-Infra-Guard skill scanner misses compiled Python bytecode
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Tencent AI-Infra-Guard's skill-scan component hardcodes __pycache__ directories and .pyc, .pyo, and .pyd extensions into skip lists. Attackers can distribute skills with benign source files and malicious compiled bytecode that executes on import while the scanner reports a safe verdict.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and government vulnerability database
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Skill and plugin scanners are release-gate controls; unchecked executable payload classes can invalidate a reported safe verdict.

upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Skill scanning blind spot and executable artifact gate.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from two public advisory sources.

qualifying_findings.title: claude-skill-antivirus ignores executable files in local skill directories
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: claude-skill-antivirus reads only SKILL.md when scanning local skill directories and ignores Python source, bytecode, and other artifacts in scripts directories. Attackers can ship malicious code outside the manifest and still receive a SAFE verdict with a 100/100 trust score.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and government vulnerability database
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Manifest-only review is insufficient for agent skill supply chains; scanners need full artifact coverage and safe-verdict provenance.

qualifying_findings.title: agentverus-scanner can certify malicious compiled companion bytecode
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: agentverus-scanner fails to analyze compiled Python bytecode files in companion code directories. Attackers can ship malicious __pycache__ entries alongside benign source files and obtain a CERTIFIED verdict with high trust scores in static and semantic analysis modes.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and government vulnerability database
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-agent certification pipelines can be bypassed when executable artifacts are omitted from analysis, creating a false security signal for downstream operators.
